children: Shares of Frequency Electronics surged after the company posted higher profit and revenue in its fiscal first quarter, putting it on track to meet its long-term financial guidance.
The stock gained 28% to $79.22 in after-hours trading on Thursday. Through the regular session's close, shares are up 90% in the past year.
The company after the bell reported net income of $4.22 million, or 41 cents a share, for its three months ended July 31, compared with $634,000, or 7 cents a share, a year earlier.
Revenue soared 70% to $23.5 million. The company's funded backlog reached a record $129 million at the end of the quarter, up 82% year over year.

"As we told you on our fourth-quarter 2026 earnings call in July, we expect to return to growth starting in this current fiscal 2027, and this first quarter is a strong proof point of that," Chief Executive Tom McClelland said.
The performance also bodes well for Frequency Electronics to meet or exceed its long-term revenue outlook, which calls for at least $150 million in annual sales by fiscal 2029, he added.
